sentences.text:
The Indian Penal Code vs In Re : Murari Lal Khandelwal on 11
November, 2024
 11.11.2024
 22
 sdas
 Allowed
 C.R.M. (A) No. 3729 of 2024

In Re:- An application for anticipatory bail under Se
 482 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita in connection
 with Bidhannagar North Police Station Case No. 95 of 2023
 dated 14.06.2023 under Sections 420/406/465/468/471/34 of
 the Indian Penal Code.
 And

In Re : Murari Lal Khandelwal ..... petitioner
 Mr. Sabyasachi Banerjee
 Mr. Apalak Basu
 Mr. Lalit Baid
 Ms. Saberi Saha
 Ms. Sanjana Shaw
 ...... for the petitioner
 Mr. Arindam Jana
 Mr. Bikram Banerjee
 Mr. Sumanta Ganguly
 Mr. Somshumbhra Ganguly
 Mr. Sevak Kundu
 Mr. Baibhav Roy
 .....for the de facto complainant
 Mr. Rudradipta Nandy, learned App
 Mr. Karan Bafuli
 ....for the State
 1.
Learned Counsel for the petitioner submits he is a businessman.

He and others had purchased 3000
shares of M/s. Addlife India Private Limited from the de facto complainant and her husband.

Share
were transferred to their names and the management of the company changed hands.

Thereafter
they sold the land owned by the company for valuable consideration to third parties.

After a lapse of
two years Fir Signed By :

Shantanu Das High Court of Calcutta 13 th of November 2024 11:57:30 Am has
been registered alleging fraud and cheating.

He is ready and willing to co-operate
with investigation and prays for anticipatory bail.

2. Learned Counsel for the de facto complainant submits she is an elderly lady and one of the
accused is a police officer.

Owing to his influence and coercion, she and her husband were compelled
to sign documents on the false promise that they were shown as "dead persons" in the records of the
Registrar of Companies.

Subsequently, when the petitioner and others were contacted for return of
documents they refused and demanded money.
Finding no alternative Fir came to be lodged.
3. Learned Counsel for the State opposes the prayer for anticipatory bail.
4. We have considered the materials on record.
Crux of the allegation in the Fir is that petitioner

and others had entered into a conspiracy and induced to the elderly couple to sign documents which
were utilized to transfer shares of M/s. Addlife India Private Limited which is the owner of a
valuable parcel of land.
Subsequently land was conveyed to third parties.

5. In the Fir it is alleged petitioner had induced the de facto complainant and her husband to sign
on papers stating they were shown as "dead persons" in the Registrar of Companies.

De facto
complainant and her husband signed on "share transfer application" which clearly shows that shares
are Signed By :
Shantanu Das High Court of Calcutta 13 th of November 2024 11:57:30 Am being
transferred by one living person to another.

Materials on records show that the de
facto complainant's husband though elderly was involved in business and it is
expected he was fully aware of the manner in which transfer of shares take place.
6.

In this backdrop it is difficult for us to believe de facto complainant and her husband were
induced to sign share transfer documents on the plea that their names were incorrectly recorded as
"dead persons" in the Registrar of Companies.

Be that as it may, transaction took place in 2021 and
no contemporaneous complaint was filed.
After a lapse of two years, Fir came to be registered.
There is substantial delay in lodging Fir.
7. It is contended report from the corporate affairs shows that the share transfer is illegal.

This may
be addressed by the complainant before the appropriate forum in accordance with law.

8. Mr. Jana, also contends petitioner had made multiple applications for anticipatory bail before the
sessions court.

Even after the first application was rejected police did not arrest the petitioner and
he had the opportunity to file subsequent applications.

We would have otherwise taken a grim view
of the matter but we note Fir is a belated one and petitioner appears to have co-operated with the
investigation.

Under such circumstances, we are inclined to grant anticipatory bail to the petitioner.
Signed By :

The Indian Penal Code vs In Re : Murari Lal Khandelwal on 11 November, 2024
Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/168790016/
2

Shantanu Das High Court of Calcutta 13 th of November 2024 11:57:30 Am
6.

Accordingly, we direct that in the event of arrest the petitioner shall be released on
bail upon furnishing a bond of Rs.50,000/-, with two sureties of like amount each, to
the satisfaction of the arresting officer and also be subject to the conditions as laid
down under Section 482(2) of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita and on
condition he shall appear before the jurisdictional court and pray for regular bail
within a period of four weeks from date and on further condition that petitioner shall
report to the investigating agency onc
e in a fortnight until further orders.
7. The application for anticipatory bail is, thus, allowed.

(Ajay Kumar Gupta, J.) (Joymalya Bagchi, J.) Signed By :
SHANTANU DAS High Court of Calcutta 13 th of November 2024 11:57:30 AM The Indian Penal Code vs In Re : Murari Lal Khandelwal on 11 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/168790016/
